decisions.reason: This secure document-storage feature builds directly on the firm's digital identity and security know-how, so even with only a 2023 launch mention it is close enough to core capabilities to be worth refining rather than removing.

An identity-bound payment wallet fits the firm's established strengths in IAM, payments, and secure customer platforms, giving management strong absorptive capacity to learn and improve it commercially.

Although NFC-tag login adds a somewhat more device-centric element than the firm's main software-platform business, it still relies on core authentication expertise and is likely to be retained while the firm tests adoption.

A secure payment and wallet framework is highly related to the firm's existing payment, identity, and platform capabilities, and its own dedicated page signals meaningful commitment and low withdrawal risk.

This secure multi-service mobile-app platform is almost exactly aligned with the firm's stated strategic direction toward super apps and ecosystems, making it very unlikely to be taken off the market.

An application-shielding security library draws on the firm's long-standing application-security expertise, and its own page suggests enough strategic relevance that management would keep developing it rather than drop it.
